issues.description: The problem statement and UML require addGuestStudents(int, String) (an int plus a reason String), but the solution implements addGuestStudents with only a single int parameter. This parameter mismatch means the solution does not match the specified API and will confuse students about the required method signature and how to use the reason parameter. It also prevents students from using the solution as a correct reference implementation for the required method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's method signature match the specification: change the solution to implement public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and (optionally) use or store the reason (e.g., log it or add a comment). Alternatively, if the intention was a single-parameter method, update the problem statement and UML to require addGuestStudents(int) so all artifacts match.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a method addGuestStudents(int, String) (an integer number of new guest students plus a String reason), but the solution repository implements addGuestStudents(int) with only a single int parameter. This mismatch in method signature (missing the String parameter) creates a mapping confusion: students following the UML or tests expecting the two-parameter variant may not find the expected method in the solution/template, and may be unsure whether the reason parameter is required or optional.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across artifacts. Implement addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) in the template and solution (or update the problem/UML to require a single-parameter addGuestStudents(int) if the reason is not needed). Preferably update the solution to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) { this.numberOfGuestStudents += numberOfNewGuestStudents; /* optionally log or store reason */ } so it matches the problem statement and UML.
